subject.title: Visible inbound channel turn can be silently dropped: zero-payload dispatch has no retry, dead-letter, or user-visible failure

question: For a visible user turn that ends with no queued reply payload, which outcomes may safely produce an automatic retry, durable recovery record, or user-facing resend notice without risking duplicate tool or channel effects?
rationale: The report spans multiple terminal causes with different safety properties; the repository policy treats fallback and compatibility behavior as a product decision rather than an implementation convenience.

options.title: Instrument first, repair proven loss branches
options.body: Add a structured outcome reason and targeted tests, then add narrow recovery only for causes that prove the original turn never ran or never delivered.

options.title: Send a generic resend notice
options.body: Reply with a minimal failure notice for all unexplained visible zero-payload outcomes, accepting that some intentional or duplicate paths may become noisy.

options.title: Adopt durable deferred recovery
options.body: Persist eligible inbound turns for later drain with explicit idempotency and delivery ownership, accepting a broader state and upgrade design.

recommendation.title: Instrument first, repair proven loss branches
recommendation.body: Add a structured outcome reason and targeted tests, then add narrow recovery only for causes that prove the original turn never ran or never delivered.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged adjacent repair explicitly chose a user-visible error over unsafe replay at the same no-reply boundary.
